content_preview.title: Chinese-Linked AI Agents Autonomously Found and Exploited a MONAI Label Zero-Day to Seize a University Server, Amazon Says
content_preview.summary: Amazon says a suspected Chinese-nexus actor let AI agents run a 48-hour hacking campaign that found and exploited a zero-day in MONAI Label with no step-by-step human direction.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Amazon's Threat Intelligence team says a suspected Chinese-nexus actor ran a roughly 48-hour hacking campaign in which autonomous AI agents, not the human operator, found and exploited a previously unknown vulnerability in an open-source application, according to a [report published on the AWS Security Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/chinese-nexus-actors-cairn-ai-agents-found-a-zero-day-on-their-own/) by Amazon CISO CJ Moses. editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Context) at 1,073 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Neutral tone throughout; attribution consistently hedged ('Amazon says', 'Amazon Threat Intelligence assesses with moderate/high confidence', 'Amazon infers'). No AI self-reference. No sensationalism despite the dramatic subject matter.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources read from local gzip snapshots after sha256 integrity verification (all four decompressed hashes matched manifest.json exactly: source-0 aws.amazon.com a2c4da47..., source-1 theregister.com fbb0c68c..., source-2 nvd.nist.gov 069aab36..., source-3 github.com da88932b...). source-0 (AWS Security Blog, CJ Moses, 'Chinese-nexus actor's Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own') and source-1 (The Register, Jessica Lyons, published Fri 20 Nov 2026 17:30 UTC) rendered as full article text and were read completely. source-2 (NVD CVE-2026-133968 page) snapshot is an empty Angular SPA shell (title 'NVD - Home', no CVE content — confirmed by grep, no '9.8' or 'CVE-2026-133968' string present in the raw HTML beyond SVG path coordinates that coincidentally contain '9.8'). Per the 'sources you could not snapshot' procedure, fetched the live NVD REST API directly instead (https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0?cveId=CVE-2026-133968, HTTP 200, independent of the reader/summarizer) and separately fetched CISA's raw KEV JSON feed (https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json, HTTP 200) and located the CVE-2026-133968 record directly in the parsed JSON — both read as raw structured data, not via a model-mediated summary. source-3 (GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94, published by ericspod, Nov 18, 2026) rendered and read in full. Anthropic disclosure: not required - story subject is Amazon/AWS, Cairn, MONAI Label and a Chinese-nexus actor; no Anthropic or Anthropic-operated product appears in the headline, summary, lead, or elsewhere.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Quote-by-quote audit of every double-quoted string in the article against the raw AWS blog and Register snapshots: (1) 'obtain shell access' - verbatim, AWS post. (2) 'Neither operation succeeded, yet together they show that the agents kept adapting for nearly a full day without human direction' - verbatim, attributed to Moses, appears identically in both AWS and Register. (3) 'The agents identified the application's framework, mapped its API endpoints, and found an upload endpoint with a filename parameter' - verbatim in both AWS and Register. (4) 'did not correspond to any assigned security advisory and was unpatched' - verbatim, AWS. (5) 'Together, these cases show that this autonomous AI agent framework is being adopted in both espionage and criminal operations' - verbatim, AWS and Register. (6) 'government partner' - verbatim phrase from AWS ('AWS worked with a government partner to notify the organizations'). (7) 'to varying degrees' (re: 27 companies) - verbatim, Register quoting Gambit Security's findings. (8) NVD quote 'in the wild starting in September 2026' - verbatim match to the live NVD API description field. No hallucinated or misattributed quotes found. Timeline/numbers verified directly against the raw AWS post: ~48-hour campaign window beginning Sept 8, discovered Sept 10 (AWS: 'approximately 48-hour period beginning September 8, 2026'; discovery 'On September 10, 2026') - matches; the ~11-minute path-traversal-to-arbitrary-file-write figure (AWS: 'In about 11 minutes, the agents went from mapping the application's API to arbitrarily writing files on the server') - matches; two failed operations (16-hour/148-action Redis op, 6+-hour GPU-server credential-spray op) versus the one successful MONAI Label exploitation - matches AWS's own structure exactly ('Neither operation succeeded' refers to the two; the zero-day operation is described separately as succeeding). CVE-2026-133968 / CVSS / KEV verified independently against raw government data, not the writer's self-reported audit: live NVD API confirms CVSS 3.1 base score 9.8, baseSeverity CRITICAL (matches article's '9.8 base score on the CVSS 3.1 scale', correctly NOT rounded up to 10.0 or called 'maximum-severity'); live NVD API cisaExploitAdd='2026-11-23' and cisaActionDue='2026-11-26' match the article's 'added to CISA's KEV catalog on November 23, 2026, with a federal patch deadline of November 26' exactly; independently fetched raw CISA KEV JSON feed confirms the same dateAdded/dueDate for CVE-2026-133968. GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94 verified: published Nov 18 2026 (matches), affected <=0.8.5 / patched 0.8.6 (matches 'before 0.8.6' and 'fix shipped in version 0.8.6'), endpoints PUT /datastore/image and PUT /datastore/label (matches), auth disabled by default (matches), credits '@aws-sec-vdp' as reporter (matches article's modest framing 'an AWS security-disclosure account' - correctly NOT overstated as 'Amazon's own security vulnerability disclosure program'). One data-provenance note, not an article error: the GHSA page's own sidebar widget displays 'CVE ID: No known CVE' (GitHub's advisory metadata appears not yet synced to the CVE assignment at snapshot time), but the live NVD record for CVE-2026-133968 independently lists this exact GHSA URL as a reference, and CISA's KEV feed lists the same GHSA URL in its notes field for this CVE - two independent government sources corroborate that this advisory documents the CVE, so the article's framing ('The flaw is now tracked as CVE-2026-133968 ... documented in GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94') holds even though GitHub's own UI widget lagged. Two previously-identified issues (writer self-reported fixing them before submission) both verified fixed in the final text: CVSS correctly stated as 9.8/critical, never 'maximum-severity' or rounded to 10.0; aws-sec-vdp correctly described as 'an AWS security-disclosure account', never 'Amazon's own security vulnerability disclosure program'.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive throughout. Confidence levels (moderate for attribution, high for zero-day assessment) are carried through from the source rather than flattened into certainty. 'Seize a university server' in the headline is a fair compression of 'gain full control of a server' / 'established a reverse shell running as root' from the AWS post, not sensationalized beyond the source's own framing.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Herald coverage of Cairn or this MONAI Label CVE found (checked src/content/articles/2026-11/ and grepped the whole archive for 'cairn'/'monai' with no hits). The three 'Context' paragraph links (DIVD/Zammad zero-days, Google GTIG's first criminal AI-built zero-day, the earlier Amazon FortiGate warning) are distinct, previously-published incidents and all three link targets were confirmed to exist on disk (src/content/articles/2026-10/02-dutch-..., 2026-05/22-google-gtig-..., 2026-02/23-ai-augmented-threat-actor-...). This is a genuinely new story, not a rewrite.
concerns: The GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94 advisory page's own 'CVE ID' field reads 'No known CVE' at snapshot time, an apparent GitHub-side metadata sync lag; independently corroborated via live NVD and CISA KEV data that this advisory does correspond to CVE-2026-133968, so no correction is warranted, but noting it for the record.

'Amazon CISO CJ Moses' is a slight simplification of his actual title (CISO of Amazon Integrated Security per his AWS bio); The Register's own piece uses the identical shorthand ('Amazon CISO CJ Moses'), so this is a widely-used characterization rather than a Herald error.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Rigorously sourced News piece on a sensitive nation-state AI-agent attribution story. Every direct quote verified verbatim against raw AWS Security Blog and Register snapshots; every timeline figure (48-hour window, 11-minute path-traversal-to-file-write, two failed operations vs. one successful) confirmed against the raw AWS post rather than the writer's self-reported audit; CVE-2026-133968's CVSS score and KEV catalog dates independently confirmed against live NVD API and raw CISA KEV JSON feed (not just the broken NVD page snapshot or the writer's claims). Both previously-flagged overstatements (CVSS rounded to 'maximum-severity'/10.0, and aws-sec-vdp mischaracterized as Amazon's own disclosure program) are confirmed fixed in the submitted text. No fabrications, no misattributions, no orphan sources, clean provenance. Featured candidacy: 2 - a well-documented escalation (AI agents autonomously discovering and weaponizing a zero-day with no step-by-step human direction) in a pattern of nation-state AI-agent offensive activity the Herald has tracked all year, reported first-hand by AWS's own threat intelligence team and independently corroborated by The Register; broad audience relevance across AI safety and cybersecurity readers, though not a first-of-its-kind event given prior DIVD/Google GTIG coverage.
